definitions.gloss: to propose, to suggest, to make overtures
definitions.explanation: To bring up a proposal or suggestion to someone, often implying an attempt to persuade or negotiate.

examples.japanese: {彼|かれ}は{私|わたし}に{新|あたら}しいビジネスの{話|はなし}を{持|も}ちかけてきた。
examples.english: He came to me with a new business proposal.

examples.japanese: {取引先|とりひきさき}から{共同|きょうどう}{開発|かいはつ}の{話|はなし}を{持|も}ちかけられた。
examples.english: Our business partner proposed a joint development project.

examples.japanese: {怪|あや}しい{投資話|とうしばなし}を{持|も}ちかける{詐欺|さぎ}に{注意|ちゅうい}。
examples.english: Be careful of scams that approach you with suspicious investment proposals.

notes:
TRANSITIVITY: {他動詞|たどうし} (transitive).

COMPOUND VERB: Formed from {持|も}つ (to hold) + かける (to apply/bring to). The combination conveys bringing something (usually a proposal) to someone.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
・{話|はなし}を{持|も}ちかける (bring up a topic/proposal)
・{相談|そうだん}を{持|も}ちかける (approach with a consultation)
・{取引|とりひき}を{持|も}ちかける (propose a deal)
・{縁談|えんだん}を{持|も}ちかける (propose a marriage arrangement)

USAGE: Often used with passive form {持|も}ちかけられる when receiving a proposal. Can have slightly negative nuance when describing unsolicited or suspicious proposals.
